factual_claims.claim: AS Tallinna Sadam’s financial performance weakened in the first six months of 2026 despite modest revenue growth.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Management Report states: 'The Group of AS Tallinna Sadam generated higher revenue in the first 6 months of 2026. However, the increase in operating expenses... had a negative impact on the Group’s financial performance.' Operating profit fell 25.7% and profit for the period fell 41.7% despite 2.4% revenue growth.

factual_claims.source_evidence: Interim Condensed Consolidated Statement of Comprehensive Income shows revenue of EUR 59,262k (59.262 million) vs EUR 57,862k (57.862 million) for H1 2026 vs H1 2025. verified_key_information_units.information: Revenue increased by EUR 1.4 million (2.4%) to EUR 59.3 million in H1 2026, with segment breakdowns of Passenger harbours (+2.9%), Cargo harbours (–2.5%), Ferry (+1.7%), and Other (+19.0%). Key drivers included higher charter fees from the icebreaker Botnica (EUR 0.9 million, +18.2%), increased electricity sales (EUR 0.6 million, +25.0%), and growth in ferry services revenue (EUR 0.3 million, +1.9%).
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Management Report pages 4-5, 6; KPI Table page 4; Segment Reporting tables pages 8-9

candidate_sentences.text: Revenue increased by EUR 1.4 million, or 2.4%, to EUR 59.3 million, supported mainly by higher charter income from the icebreaker Botnica, increased electricity sales and growth in ferry service revenue.
Revenue rose across the Passenger harbours, Ferry and Other segments, but declined 2.5% in Cargo harbours.

verified_key_information_units.information: Operational volumes declined significantly: cargo handling fell 5.0% to 6.5 million tonnes (mainly due to liquid bulk down 33.8%), passengers decreased 2.0% to 3.6 million (with the Tallinn–Helsinki route down 2.6%), and vessel calls dropped 4.8%.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Operating Volumes section pages 4-6; KPI Table page 4

candidate_sentences.text: Cargo volumes declined 5.0% to 6.5 million tonnes, mainly because liquid bulk fell 33.8%.
Passenger numbers decreased 2.0% to 3.6 million, although cruise passengers increased 47.8%.

verified_key_information_units.information: Operating expenses rose EUR 3.9 million (24.0%) in H1 2026, primarily from fuel costs up EUR 1.4 million (47.6%) due to higher prices and severe ice conditions, electricity costs up EUR 0.7 million (28.8%), and technical maintenance/repair expenses up EUR 1.2 million (80.0%).

candidate_sentences.text: Operating expenses increased by EUR 3.9 million, or 24.0%, to EUR 20.2 million.
Fuel costs rose 47.6% to EUR 4.4 million because of higher diesel prices and more severe ice conditions, while electricity costs increased 28.8% to EUR 3.1 million.

Technical maintenance and repair costs rose 80.0% to EUR 2.8 million, partly reflecting more extensive repairs to Botnica, ferries and harbour infrastructure, while the comparative period benefited from a EUR 0.9 million insurance indemnity.

verified_key_information_units.information: Operating profit decreased by EUR 4.7 million (25.7%) to EUR 13.6 million and profit for the period declined by EUR 4.3 million (41.7%) to EUR 6.0 million. Adjusted EBITDA fell EUR 4.0 million (13.5%) to EUR 25.8 million, mainly due to higher operating expenses, lower cargo/passenger volumes, and the absence of prior-year one-off gains (land sale profit and insurance indemnity).
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Management Report pages 4-5, 7-8; KPI Table page 4

candidate_sentences.text: Operating profit fell by EUR 4.7 million, or 25.7%, to EUR 13.6 million, reducing the operating margin from 31.6% to 22.9%.
Adjusted EBITDA declined 13.5% to EUR 25.8 million, with the margin decreasing from 51.5% to 43.5%.
Profit before tax fell 27.3% to EUR 11.4 million, while profit for the period decreased 41.7% to EUR 6.0 million.
Overall, higher costs, weaker cargo and passenger volumes, and the absence of prior-year one-off gains outweighed revenue growth.

verified_key_information_units.information: Investments totalled EUR 3.5 million in H1 2026 (versus EUR 12.0 million in H1 2025), mainly for ferry engine replacement, upgrades to the quay at Paldiski South Harbour, and IT infrastructure. Q2 investments were EUR 2.3 million (versus EUR 8.4 million in Q2 2025).

candidate_sentences.text: Investments fell 70.6% to EUR 3.5 million.

details.completeness_justification: All HIGH importance criteria (K1-K4, K6) are fully present. K5 (MEDIUM) is present. K7 (HIGH) is partially present: Botnica's North Sea project (S3), the EUR 19.2 million dividend (S16), and the EUR 32 million loan (S23) are covered, but the Tallinn City Council plan for Terminal A/D areas and the Regula ferry order are missing. K8 (MEDIUM) is entirely missing (no market cap, share price, or shareholder data). The overall picture is captured with only one fully missing criterion (K8) and one partially covered criterion (K7), justifying a 'Yes' rating.
details.coherence_justification: The candidate summary is internally coherent with no material contradictions or logical gaps. All statements build logically upon each other: revenue growth is qualified by segment performance (S2, S4), cost increases are explained with specific drivers (S5-S8, S13), and profitability declines are consistently tied to these cost pressures and volume weaknesses (S11-S13, S15, S24). The summary maintains clear organization with progressive cause-effect relationships, and there is no unnecessary repetition. While S17 ('Operating activity was mixed') is somewhat vague, it does not contradict any other statements and serves as a valid transitional phrase to the subsequent operational details (S18-S19). The arithmetic relationships between segment figures and consolidated totals are not claimed to be exhaustive additive components, so differences do not constitute contradictions under the specified evaluation rules.
